name: Roomba Combo j9+ (US)

radios.note: iRobot's page says the robot needs a Wi-Fi connection and a software update before first use. The Wi-Fi band was not confirmed on an iRobot page.

matter.note: No Matter statement found on iRobot pages or a CSA listing. iRobot's later Matter rollouts named other models (Combo 10 Max, Roomba Plus 500 Combo, Max 700), not the Combo j9+.

apple_home.note: iRobot says the robot can pair with Siri; that is voice control, not a Home app accessory. Apple Home support not confirmed.

google_home.note: iRobot says the robot can be paired with Google Assistant.

alexa.note: iRobot says the robot can be paired with Alexa.

smartthings.note: No iRobot or Samsung page found for SmartThings.

home_assistant.note: The official Roomba integration page does not list the j9+ among tested models and says newer x05 Wi-Fi models do not work. j9+ support not confirmed.

hubRequired.note: The Clean Base Auto-Fill dock is not a hub.

localControl.note: No maker statement on local-only control found.

cleaning.note: Combo model that vacuums and mops.

suctionPa.note: iRobot's pages we saw do not state suction in pascals.

selfEmptying.note: Clean Base Auto-Fill dock empties debris for up to 60 days and refills liquid.

summary: iRobot says the Roomba Combo j9+ pairs with Alexa and Google Assistant, and no Matter support turned up. It vacuums and mops with camera-based PrecisionVision navigation, and the Clean Base Auto-Fill dock empties debris for up to 60 days and refills the liquid.
caveats: iRobot mentions Siri, but that is voice control, not a Home app accessory, so Apple Home isn't confirmed.
No Matter statement exists on iRobot's pages or in the CSA listing; later iRobot Matter rollouts named other models.
The official Home Assistant Roomba integration doesn't list the j9+ and says newer x05 Wi-Fi models don't work.
